templates.title: an instant is one simultaneous moment

templates.text: An instant is one moment the game treats as simultaneous. A turn boundary the adoption can construct is an instant like any other; where there is no turn boundary, that clause asserts nothing.

templates.title: waiting and active events are distinguishable

when: the event enters the waiting set and is selected
then: before selection it is recorded as a waiting event that has not begun
during ordered effect application it is recorded as the active event
the active event visits an effect boundary before its first effect

templates.text: A waiting event is accepted but has not begun. An active event is applying ordered effects. Every active event visits an effect boundary before its first effect.

where no ending event exists, this test asserts nothing

templates.text: Each ending event the adoption can construct follows the ordinary event lifecycle but records no outcome when it resolves. Only step 15 records an outcome, after the waiting set is empty. Where none exists, this test asserts nothing.

templates.title: container order never decides event resolution

then: the two runs select and resolve the same events in the same declared order
no event order is taken from container order or document order

templates.text: Changing container order or document order without changing declarations never changes event resolution. Rank, a rank tie, and within-class order decide the sequence; document order never does. Step 5 says container order in the adoption file never selects an event.

templates.title: an accepted proposal commits once and creates one event

test.given: a valid proposal with distinguishable payload values, event class, due instant, and an ordinary cost where its Fixed rule declares one
when: the proposal is accepted and its event is admitted

one event payload is created once and enters its declared event class at its due instant
the payload contains every value required to survive later source loss, while uncaptured state is read only when an effect resolves
where later source loss cannot be constructed, the payload-survival observation asserts nothing

templates.text: An accepted proposal creates one payload once and enters its declared event class at its due instant. Where it has an ordinary cost, that cost commits once at the point its rule names; otherwise the cost clause asserts nothing. The payload captures every value that must survive later source loss; where no such loss can occur, that observation asserts nothing.

templates.title: a new event uses the interrupt path or caused-event path

a branch the adoption cannot construct asserts nothing and no event uses both paths

templates.text: After an instant opens, a valid declared interrupt enters only through the interrupt path. Every other newly created event due now follows caused-events. An unavailable branch asserts nothing, and no event uses both paths.

templates.title: the lowest eligible rank resolves first

templates.text: Within {{row.class-id}}, lower {{row.index-name}} resolves first. Where the row names a second index, equal first numbers resolve by it; otherwise equal first numbers cannot arise or cannot change the result.
